title: LLM routing + prefetch: cost-aware prefetching brainstorm
content:
Goal:
- Rough brain dump for a cost-aware prefetching feature that plugs into Smart Routing. Aim: reduce serving unit costs for common prefixes while keeping P95 latency within SLOs.

Background / motivation:
- Many requests share prefixes (system prompts, instruction templates). If we can prefetch KV cache or do early token generation on cheaper capacity, we can amortize decode cost.
- Current routing picks model/variant by latency/cost tier but has no tight feedback loop for upstream prefetch decisions.
- Want a low-risk opt-in path: feature flags per-customer / per-route, conservative TTLs, measurable ROI.

Key ideas (brainstorm):
1) Passive KV prefetch: detect repeated prefixes, warm KV cache on same worker when new request arrives (cheap)
   - pros: low complexity, no extra tokens generated
   - cons: only helps if subsequent request hits same worker (need sticky routing or shard-aware cache)
2) Active prefix prefetch (early decode): for top-k frequent prefixes, trigger short decode on a lower-cost model/quantized variant to produce KV cache for warm workers
   - pros: broader hit rate, can use cheaper variants (int8/q4)
   - cons: extra compute spent speculatively; must be cost-aware
3) Hybrid: use passive when hit-rate likely high; use active prefetch for tail heavy prefixes where passive fails

Signals to use for decisioning:
- prefix frequency (rolling window 1h/24h)
- per-route latency SLA and P95 headroom
- model variant compatibility (can we prefetch with q4 and reuse on fp16?)
- worker locality / routing policy (is sticky routing enabled?)
- expected cost delta (prefetch compute vs expected savings from avoided cold-start decode)

User stories:
- As an ML infra engineer, I want an opt-in prefetch config per-route so I can test cost/latency tradeoffs on staging before enabling in prod.
- As a product developer, I want rollouts (canary) so we can gradually enable prefetch for 1%/10%/100% of traffic.
- As an SRE, I want visibility in Console: prefetch hit rate, cost saved, extra compute burned, P95 delta, and regressions flagged.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- admin config: per-route toggle + prefetch mode (passive|active|hybrid) + sampling rate
- lightweight telemetry: prefetch attempts, prefetch hits, upstream cost estimate, incurred prefetch cost
- A/B dashboard: show cost per token and P95 before/after for the route
- Safeguard: automatic disable if P95 increases > X ms or error rate increases

Open questions / tradeoffs (TODO):
- Prefetch model compatibility: can we reuse a KV cache generated by a quantized model for a higher precision model? Need experiments (Jordan has a branch touching KV serialization).
- Routing implications: passive prefetch only helps if requests land on same worker. Should we add a weak sticky routing for prefetched routes? Impact on load distribution?
- Cost accounting: how to attribute speculative compute costs to customer vs platform? For hosted API, probably platform bears it unless customer opts in to pay for prefetch. For Dedicated, expose a metric/flag.
- Security/data residency: do we ever prefetch for routes with customer data that shouldn’t be cached/shared? Need to respect private-deployments flags and KMS policies.

Rough cost math (back-of-envelope):
- typical decode cost for prefix of length 40 tokens = X tokens * cost_per_token_model = 40 * $0.00002 = $0.0008 (example numbers)
- if 10k requests/day share prefix A and prefetch hit rate 20%, savings = 2000 * 40 * cost_per_token = 2000*40*0.00002 = $1.6/day, but speculative prefetch compute for active prefetch might be 500 prefetches/day => 500*40*0.00001 (cheaper variant) = $0.2/day -> net $1.4/day. Need real numbers from billing team.

Instrumentation / experiments to run:
- Feature: prefix frequency detector + dashboard; run passive prefetch on small subset of routes to measure natural worker-local hit rate
- Experiment 1: passive-only for 7 days on 5 routes; collect hit rate and latency impact
- Experiment 2: active prefetch using quantized variant on same routes; measure cost vs hit rate
- Experiment 3: hybrid with sticky routing enabled vs none; measure load imbalance

Implementation notes / integration points:
- Serving runtime: KV cache APIs + hooks to trigger prefetch; need safe non-blocking prefetch path (no client-perceived latency increase)
- Smart router: new decision function to consult prefetching policy; potentially add a ‘prefetch hint’ header
- Console: add telemetry + rollout controls (percent-based) + guard rails UI
- Billing: create meter for prefetch compute so we can attribute/cap costs for Dedicated customers

Next steps (short):
- Sync with Raja and Priya on feasibility (KV compatibility + routing) — scheduled sync 2025-01-14
- Add baseline telemetry PR (low-risk) to master branch: prefix frequency detector + event stream
- Open JIRA RR-3421 with tasks: experiments, runtime hooks, UI flags, billing meter

Notes to self:
- keep language conservative in docs: "opt-in" and "experimental" until we have 2-week experiment results
- check with security about caching customer-generated prompts by default (probably need opt-in for PII-sensitive routes)

Links / references:
- earlier scratch: users/llm-prefetch-kv-cache-scratchpad.json (look up for prior experiments)
- relevant PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/824 (KV serialize change)

Unresolved items to decide in design doc:
- pricing model for hosted: platform absorbs prefetch cost vs bill as premium feature
- TTL semantics: how long do we keep a prefetched KV cache before evicting? per-route config?
- migration story for Dedicated: expose cap on speculative compute in tenant config

End of brainstorm. This is a rough scratchpad — will turn into a PRD outline after experiments and a short sync with Raja/Priya.
